pipelinesSetup.cloud.title: Connect a cloud
pipelinesSetup.cloud.intro: Bemmoly reads and deploys only where you allow it. Connecting creates nothing in your cloud.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.gcpServices: Cloud Run, Cloud Build, Artifact Registry, Secret Manager
pipelinesSetup.cloud.mode.attachedHint: Bemmoly deploys into them and creates nothing.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.mode.managedHint: You run a setup script once. Pipelines then creates a project per environment inside one folder, and nowhere else.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.signIn.vmHint: Bemmoly runs on a Google Cloud VM and uses its service account. No key files.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.signIn.gcloud: A gcloud sign-in on this machine
pipelinesSetup.cloud.signIn.gcloudHint: Bemmoly runs on a laptop or a server. It acts as a service account through your gcloud sign-in, so it gets that account’s permissions, not yours.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.signIn.wifHint: Only for Bemmoly on another cloud or a Kubernetes cluster that gives its machine an identity. Most installs need one of the two above.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.reach.folder: Every project in a folder or organization
pipelinesSetup.cloud.reach.folderInvalid: Use a folder ID such as 417302018845, or organizations/ and its ID
pipelinesSetup.cloud.reach.pickField: Project IDs, separated by commas or spaces
pipelinesSetup.cloud.reach.pickInvalid: {id} is not a project ID; IDs use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens
pipelinesSetup.cloud.connected: Google Cloud connected. Nothing was created.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.name: Google Cloud
pipelinesSetup.cloud.connectedManaged: Google Cloud connected. Choose a layout in Platform › Clouds to create the projects.
pipelinesSetup.guide.title: Steps
pipelinesSetup.guide.hint: Do them in order, then check
pipelinesSetup.guide.label: Steps to connect Google Cloud
pipelinesSetup.guide.choose: Choose what Pipelines does and how Bemmoly signs in, and the steps appear here.
pipelinesSetup.guide.optional: Only if Bemmoly runs in Docker
pipelinesSetup.guide.fillIn: Fill in {fields} to see the command.
pipelinesSetup.guide.fillReach: Choose what Bemmoly can reach to see the command.
pipelinesSetup.guide.suggested: Suggested. Change it if you like.
pipelinesSetup.guide.where.cloudShell: Run it in Cloud Shell, signed in as an administrator.
pipelinesSetup.guide.where.thisMachine: Run it in a terminal on the machine Bemmoly runs on. A browser opens for you to sign in.
pipelinesSetup.guide.where.compose: Run it in the folder that holds Bemmoly’s docker-compose.yml.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.bootstrapText: Creates a folder for Pipelines, a control project and the bemmoly-control service account, and gives that account roles on the folder and the billing account only. It asks before changing anything, and prints a folder ID at the end for the last step.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.tokenCreatorTe: Bemmoly uses your sign-in to act as bemmoly-control, so it gets that account’s permissions and never yours. This lets your account do that.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.serviceAccount: Make the service account Bemmoly acts as
Bemmoly uses your sign-in to act as this account, so it gets only what the last step grants. This makes the account if it does not exist yet, and lets your account act as it.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.signIn: Sign in on this machine as that account
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.signInText: Saves a sign-in that acts as the service account. Bemmoly finds it on its own; your own permissions are not used.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.docker: Let Bemmoly’s container read that sign-in
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.dockerText: A container cannot see your home folder. This mounts the gcloud folder read-only, tells Bemmoly where the sign-in is, and restarts Bemmoly.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.attachVm: Give Bemmoly’s VM the bemmoly-control account
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.attachVmText: Bemmoly signs in as its VM’s service account. Switch it to bemmoly-control in the console, or run the command instead.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.attachVmStop: Compute Engine › VM instances: open Bemmoly’s VM and choose Stop.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.attachVmEdit: When it has stopped, choose Edit.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.attachVmAccoun: Under Identity and API access, set Service account to {account}.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.attachVmScopes: Set Access scopes to Allow full access to all Cloud APIs. Scopes are an old, coarse limit; the roles the setup script granted are what limit Bemmoly.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.wifFileText: The file says how Bemmoly trades its machine’s identity for a Google one. It holds no secret.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.folderIdText: The setup script printed it at the end, after Folder ID.
pipelinesSetup.guide.step.grantText: Turns on the APIs a deploy needs and grants the deploy roles where you choose, and nowhere else. Run it as a project owner.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.organizationI: An organization ID is 6 to 20 digits.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.billingAccoun: gcloud billing accounts list shows it.
Use the billing account ID, such as 01A2B3-C4D5E6-F7A8B9.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.folderNameHin: The script creates it, or uses the one with this name.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.folderNameInv: Up to 30 letters, digits, spaces, hyphens or underscores.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.controlProjec: A new project the script creates. Project IDs are unique across Google Cloud.
6 to 30 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, starting with a letter.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.regionHint: Where services go when an environment names none.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.regionInvalid: Name a region such as us-central1.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.folderIdInval: A folder ID is 6 to 20 digits, such as 417302018845.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.youHint: The account you use with gcloud on the machine Bemmoly runs on.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.youInvalid: Use an email address, such as you@example.com.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.principalHint: The service account it uses, such as bemmoly@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.principalInva: Use the service account’s email address.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.serviceAccoun: Such as bemmoly@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com. It is made if it does not exist.
Use a service account email ending in .iam.gserviceaccount.com.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.vmNameInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.vmZoneInvalid: Name a zone such as us-central1-a.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.vmProjectHint: The project the VM is in.
pipelinesSetup.guide.field.vmProjectInva: 6 to 30 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, starting with a letter.
pipelinesSetup.guide.check.title: Check
pipelinesSetup.guide.check.text: Bemmoly signs in the way you chose and checks each step. It creates nothing.
pipelinesSetup.guide.check.notYet: Finish the steps above first: Check needs the sign-in, and {need}.
pipelinesSetup.guide.check.needFolder: the folder ID and billing account
pipelinesSetup.guide.check.stillMissing: Google Cloud is connected, but these still need doing before Pipelines can create projects:
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.notCreated: {account} does not exist yet. Run step {step}.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.cannotAct: Your account cannot act as {account} yet. Run step {step}.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.noSignIn: Bemmoly found no gcloud sign-in it can use. Run step {step}, and the Docker step if Bemmoly runs in Docker.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.actingAs: Your sign-in is acting as {principal}, not {account}. Run step {step}.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.vmNoAccount: The VM gave Bemmoly no service account to sign in with. Run step {step}.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.vmActingAs: The VM signs in as {principal}, not {account}. Run step {step}.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.fileFailed: Bemmoly could not sign in with this file. Make it again with the guide, then choose it here.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.grantsMissin: {account} is missing roles on the folder or billing account. Run step {step} again; it only adds what is missing.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.folderUnseen: Bemmoly cannot see folder {folder}. Paste the folder ID the script printed.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.folderReady: Bemmoly holds what it needs on folder {folder}.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.noProjects: Bemmoly signed in but found no projects there. Check what it can reach, run step {step}, then check again.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.blocked: {count, plural, one {# project needs} other {# projects need}} access. Run step {step}, then check again, or connect now and fix it later.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.projectsRead: Bemmoly can deploy to {count, plural, one {# project} other {# projects}}.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.grantedOther: Bemmoly signs in as {principal}, but the command grants {expected}. Change it in step {step}, run it, then check again.
pipelinesSetup.guide.report.machineFaile: Bemmoly could not sign in as this machine. On a Google Cloud VM, give the VM a service account; elsewhere, choose another way to sign in.
pipelinesSetup.wif.consoleLink: Get it from the Google Cloud console
pipelinesSetup.wif.notJson: That file is not JSON. Choose the file the console downloaded.
pipelinesSetup.wif.isKey: That is a service account key. Bemmoly never takes keys; make a workload identity file instead.
pipelinesSetup.wif.notFederation: That is not a workload identity file. Its type should be external_account.
pipelinesSetup.wif.onVm: Bemmoly on a Google Cloud VM? Choose ‘The machine Bemmoly runs on’. On a laptop? Choose ‘A gcloud sign-in on this machine’. Neither needs this file.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step1: IAM and admin › Workload Identity Federation › Create pool, named bemmoly.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step2: Add a provider that matches where Bemmoly runs: AWS (with the account ID) for a server on AWS, or OpenID Connect (with the issuer URL) for Kubernetes, GitHub, Azure or another identity provider. Set the attribute mapping google.subject = assertion.sub.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step3: IAM and admin › Service accounts › Create service account, named bemmoly.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step4: Back on the pool, choose Grant access › Grant access using service account impersonation, pick the bemmoly account and "All identities in the pool", then Save.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step5: In the "Configure your application" dialog, pick the provider, enter the token path on Bemmoly's server, and Download config. That JSON is the file to choose here.
pipelinesSetup.wif.commandsLabel: Commands that make the workload identity file
pipelinesSetup.wif.fillIn: Type the project ID and number to fill the commands in.
pipelinesSetup.home.title: Welcome, {name}
pipelinesSetup.home.intro: Bemmoly Pipelines is empty, and nothing runs until you set it up. Do these in any order.
pipelinesSetup.step.cloudText: Pick a provider and the projects Bemmoly may reach. Nothing is created in your cloud.
pipelinesSetup.step.environmentsText: Name them, link a project to each, and set their order and rules.
pipelinesSetup.step.peopleText: Give each person a role. Make approval groups if you want approvals.
pipelinesSetup.step.servicesText: Connect GitHub and pick the services to deploy.
pipelinesSetup.step.pipelinesText: For each service: start empty, from a template, or from a file in your repository.
pipelinesSetup.step.templatesText: 4 built-in templates are ready. Add your own, and steps every pipeline must keep.
pipelinesSetup.on.title: What's switched on
pipelinesSetup.on.footer: Everything starts off. Turn on what you need, when you need it.
pipelinesSetup.startOver.title: Start over
pipelinesSetup.startOver.text: Removes every Pipelines record on this install: clouds, environments, services, pipelines, runs, versions, change requests, approval groups and roles. Work, Docs, people and your cloud itself stay as they are; nothing is deleted in your cloud.
pipelinesSetup.startOver.dialogText: This cannot be undone. Pipelines becomes a fresh install with the setup checklist.
pipelinesSetup.startOver.done: Pipelines is empty again. {count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}} removed.
